description: split.js: a session covering two genuinely distinct topics (auth middleware, then an unrelated CSS bug) with a false-boundary tempter in between (a clarifying follow-up on the same topic) — checks both real-boundary detection and the over-fragmentation guard.

turns.text: The JWT middleware is rejecting valid tokens intermittently, can you look into it?

Found it — the clock skew tolerance was set to 0, so any token issued within a couple hundred milliseconds of the server's own clock drift gets rejected as 'not yet valid'. Setting a 5-second leeway on the nbf/iat checks fixes it.
Good catch, can you also make sure the leeway doesn't apply to the exp check?
Right, exp should stay strict — only nbf/iat get the leeway. Updated the middleware so expiry is checked with zero tolerance.
Separately, the settings page's save button is misaligned on Safari, off by about 8px to the right.

That's a flexbox gap fallback issue — Safari's older versions don't support the gap property inside flex containers the way Chrome/Firefox do. Switched to margin-based spacing for that row instead, verified it renders correctly in both.
